findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - An owner moves a finding to a follow-up fix, then a later review reports the same finding again.
`review._settled` records the split as `known: Split into follow-up fix ...`, and the later review carries that reason as a dismissal (`src/forge/review.py:634` and `:1038`). This line consequently prints `Dismissed: known: Split into follow-up fix ...` even though the finding was moved to the fix. Unlike read note 11, this case has an actual follow-up fix and mislabels it after a later review.
Done-when 1 requires: “In the item's own checkout, before it merges, `forge close <item> --show` prints every finding of the latest saved review in full (title, file and line, priority, whole text) with its current state (open, dismissed or follow-up), for a part or a fix, and runs no tests, no review, no fetch and no push, and writes nothing.”

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A later change omits an advisory finding's body, swaps finding states, or contacts the remote while showing a review.
The test asserts only the first finding's body, searches for state labels independently of their findings, and never exercises a split. Its network check also reads the main checkout's `FETCH_HEAD`, while the item is a linked worktree with its own [FETCH_HEAD](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmd/pr/checkout/checkout.go). Counting `gh` calls cannot detect the `git push` used by close (`src/forge/close.py:879`). An up-to-date fetch or push can therefore run without changing any fact the test records. The sole proof can pass while these promised behaviors are broken.
